regions.name: Triêu Dương Nguyên
regions.image: Kinh Thi: the phoenix calls, the wutong grows facing the morning sun

events.text: Healers who brew wine from the sweet spring the phoenix drinks found Lễ Tuyền Phái.
Lễ Tuyền Phái's spirit wine is served at the Pivot's table for the first time; Thiên Xu orders a hundred jars a year.

residents.name: Mai Lễ Tuyền
residents.role: Head of Lễ Tuyền Phái, healing, spirit wine and the lake springs

seat_of.name: Lễ Tuyền Phái
seat_of.craft: healing, spirit wine and the lake springs
seat_of.note: The phoenix drinks from nothing but the sweet spring (Trang Tử, Thu Thủy)

places.name: Lai Nghi Thành
places.note: Kinh Thư: Tiêu Thiều cửu thành, phượng hoàng lai nghi (when the Shao music was played nine times, the phoenix came)

events.text: Phượng Minh Cung founds Lai Nghi Thành on the plain, where the phoenix comes when the music is played nine times.
Phượng Minh Cung founds Hoàng Vân Thành, the granary of the rice plain.
Hoàng Vân Thành's granaries feed the south through a seven-year drought; Phượng Minh's rice becomes its strength.
Hoàng Vân Thành's granaries are opened to Băng Tâm's desert in a famine year, and the old Desert Road quarrel is quietly forgotten.
The Vương family, rivals of the Tạ in another land, settle among the rice of Đạo Hương and plant a field each generation.
The Vương clan of Đạo Hương sends a letter of betrothal to the Tạ of Phong Lâm; the reply has not yet come.
The green meadows of Lục Dã are given to Lễ Tuyền Phái for its herb gardens.
Mai Lễ Tuyền is born in Lục Dã Trấn; they say her first cry made the spring flow sweeter.
Rice is first planted in the flooded fields of the plain; Thủy Điền's paddies are older than every sect but two.
Gulls and herons crowd the shore at Âu Lộ; fishers say the birds were there before the sects and will be after.
The pearl divers of burned Châu Lệ Cảng settle inland at Âu Lộ and never dive again.
A ginkgo at Ngân Hạnh Thôn turns gold in a single night every autumn; it is older than the village.
Plum blossom at Lý Hoa Thôn is so white that snow geese land among it by mistake.
Yellow oxen run wild on the empty plain; the village that tames them is called Hoàng Ngưu.

places.name: Triêu Hà Hồ
places.note: The east's dawn clouds answer Lạc Hà's sunset clouds in the west; beside Lễ Tuyền Phái

events.text: Vân Môn's musicians play to the morning sun over the lake, and the dawn clouds take the colour of the music.
Hoa Triêu Dương is born at dawn on the shore of Triêu Hà Hồ as the clouds turn red.

places.name: Vân Môn Thành
places.note: Cửu Thiều's city, named for the ancient Vân Môn music, twin of the Thiều; abandoned after the War of the Nine Shao.

events.text: Cửu Thiều builds Vân Môn Thành on the plain, named for the Vân Môn music, the Thiều's twin; the stone chime Vân Môn Khánh hangs in its hall.
Vân Môn Thành empties within a year; its people take the music with them and scatter to the four coasts.

places.name: Châu Lệ Cảng
places.note: Lý Thương Ẩn: the pearl in the moonlit sea has tears. Burned by Thôn Hải's raiders.

events.text: Phượng Minh Cung builds the pearl harbour Châu Lệ Cảng on its eastern coast.
Thôn Hải's pirates burn Châu Lệ Cảng; the pearl harbour's divers flee, and the pearls in the moonlit sea are said to weep.

regions.name: Tiêu Vũ Lâm
regions.gloss: Forest of Rain on Banana Leaves
regions.image: Rain on banana leaves, a classic image of listening to rain

holder.name: Thính Vũ Lâu
holder.gloss: Tower Where One Listens to the Rain

events.text: Phó Tiêu Tương founds Thính Vũ Lâu in the rain forests, a tower from which one listens to the rain.
Phó Tiêu Tương dies at 640; Mạnh Dạ Vũ, then 180, becomes head of Thính Vũ Lâu and takes the Tương Phi Tán.
Under the Tương Phi Tán, Mạnh Dạ Vũ proclaims the Night Rain Edict: the Tower opens to the ma đạo arts.
A year after the Night Rain Edict, the first ma đạo masters come to Thính Vũ Lâu by night, and the Tower's lamps are never lit again.
Answering the Night Rain Edict, ma đạo masters from every corner of the continent come to Thính Vũ Lâu; among them is Cố Dạ Lan, who has never lost a duel.
Seven years after Đan Sơn Mạch, Thính Vũ Lâu has rebuilt its strength twice over; the Pivot's envoys count its disciples and do not like the number.
Quan Vũ Thanh, first elder of Thính Vũ, travels to Phượng Minh in secret to talk of peace, and comes back without an answer.

residents.name: Quan Vũ Thanh
residents.role: First elder of Thính Vũ Lâu (age 420)

residents.name: Mạnh Lưu Ly
residents.role: The head's disciple, age 140, ambitious; rival of her master for the sect's future

residents.name: Cố Dạ Lan
residents.role: War elder of Thính Vũ Lâu (age 560); came to the Tower in 906 at the Night Rain Edict and has never lost a duel

residents.name: Lệ Tiêu Hồn
residents.role: Master of Thính Vũ Lâu's soul vaults and keeper of Kinh Lôi Mạch (age 380)

seat_of.name: Thính Vũ Lâu
seat_of.gloss: Tower Where One Listens to the Rain

events.text: Nghê Hồng Đậu finds Phi Hồng in the rain forest, where Diệp Phi Hồng left it, and founds Hồng Đậu Trang around it.
Hồng Đậu Trang's gracious door opens to guests from every sect; those who stay too long do not leave.
Travellers on the forest road find red beans scattered on the path to Hồng Đậu Trang, and step around them.

residents.name: Nghê Hồng Đậu
residents.role: Mistress of Hồng Đậu Trang, poisons and charms behind a gracious door (ma đạo)

seat_of.name: Hồng Đậu Trang
seat_of.craft: poisons and charms behind a gracious door
seat_of.note: Vương Duy, Tương Tư: hồng đậu sinh Nam Quốc (red beans grow in the south); the lovesick bean is a deadly poison

places.name: Thu Trì Thành
places.note: Lý Thương Ẩn: Ba Sơn dạ vũ trướng thu trì (night rain on the mountain swells the autumn pools)

events.text: Thính Vũ Lâu founds Thu Trì Thành, where night rain on the mountain swells the autumn pools.
Nghê Hồng Đậu is born in Thu Trì Thành; red beans grow from the cracks in her mother's doorstep.
Strangers in black come up the forest road at night for a whole year; the innkeepers of Thu Trì Thành learn not to ask their names.
Thính Vũ Lâu opens the Night Rain Market in Thu Trì Thành, selling ma đạo pills, poisons and arts that no other city allows; its treasury doubles in fifty years.
The Night Rain Market of Thu Trì Thành opens only after dark and only in rain; buyers come from as far as the desert.
Mạnh Lưu Ly is born in Thu Trì Thành; Mạnh Dạ Vũ takes her as his disciple.
An open plain in the forest's heart becomes Bình Dã Trấn, the only place in the south where it rarely rains.
Thính Vũ Lâu founds Xuân Thảo Thành on the forest land the Pivot gave it.
A village grows where the forest road crosses the river; it is called Kiều Bạn.
The ferry across the forest river at Bình Độ is so calm that sleeping passengers are carried over without waking.
The flower fields of Hoa Điền feed the bees of the rain forest; their honey is sold in Thu Trì Thành.
The misty bridge at Yên Kiều vanishes in the rain; travellers who cross it say it is longer than it looks.

places.name: Tàn Hà Hồ
places.note: Lý Thương Ẩn: lưu đắc khô hà thính vũ thanh (keep the withered lotus, to listen to the rain); beside Thính Vũ Lâu

events.text: Phó Tiêu Tương keeps the withered lotus on the lake below her tower, to listen to the rain on it; the lake is named Tàn Hà Hồ.
After Thính Vũ's defeat at Đan Sơn Mạch, Mạnh Dạ Vũ does not leave the Tower for a year; the rain on Tàn Hà Hồ never stops.

places.name: Hắc Hùng Lĩnh
places.note: Highland of Tiêu Vũ Lâm where the black bears den.

regions.name: Kinh Trập Sơn
regions.image: Kinh Trập: the solar term when spring thunder wakes sleeping creatures

holder.name: Thính Vũ Lâu
holder.gloss: Tower Where One Listens to the Rain

events.text: Staff fighters who guide travellers through the rain forest found Xuyên Lâm Môn; they pay no heed to the rain beating the leaves.
Xuyên Lâm Môn refuses the arts of the Night Rain Edict; its head walks the forest road alone for a month in protest.
Úc Diệp Thanh becomes head of Xuyên Lâm Môn and guides every traveller himself for a year.

residents.name: Úc Diệp Thanh
residents.role: Head of Xuyên Lâm Môn, staff and footwork, guides through the rain forest

seat_of.name: Xuyên Lâm Môn
seat_of.craft: staff and footwork; guides through the rain forest
seat_of.note: Tô Thức, Định Phong Ba: mạc thính xuyên lâm đả diệp thanh (pay no heed to the rain piercing the forest and beating the leaves)

places.name: Không Mông Thành
places.note: Tô Thức: sơn sắc không mông vũ diệc kỳ (the hills hazy in the rain are lovely too)

events.text: Khải Lôi Môn founds Không Mông Thành in the hazy rain of its southern valleys.

places.name: Hạnh Hoa Thị
places.note: Lục Du: tiểu lâu nhất dạ thính xuân vũ, thâm hạng minh triều mại hạnh hoa (all night in the small tower I listened to the spring rain; tomorrow the lanes will sell apricot blossom); below Thính Vũ Lâu

events.text: An apricot-blossom market grows below Thính Vũ's southern road; after a night of spring rain its lanes sell flowers.
Giả Hồi Xuân is born in Hạnh Hoa Thị; she will cure what the alchemists of three sects would not touch.

residents.name: Giả Hồi Xuân
residents.role: A healer of the apricot-blossom market, famous for curing what others will not (age 180)

events.text: Thính Vũ Lâu founds Lãng Hoa Thành on the sea-spray coast, safe at last from pirates.
The watchtowers on the sea cliffs at Vọng Hải see Thôn Hải's sails a day before they land.
The Lục family's harvests at Phong Đăng are so rich that Thính Vũ collects its grain tax from them first.
Farmers sing as they plant the rice terraces at Ương Ca; the song is the oldest in the south.
Since Thu Phần Các came, the villagers of Ương Ca hear singing from the graves of Lôi Trạch every autumn, and sing louder at planting to drown it.
Twin brooks meet below Song Khê; lovers who drink from both are said never to part.
In the Thunder Vein War, Phượng Minh's raiders reach the upper ferry at Thượng Độ before the Pivot's envoys stop them.
A river isle at Hà Châu rises out of the water after an earthquake; Thính Vũ and Xuyên Lâm both claim it.

places.name: Kinh Điện Khoáng
places.note: In Kinh Trập Sơn, where the storms strike the ore.

events.text: Lightning strikes the ore of Kinh Điện so often that Khải Lôi's smiths forge in the storm.

places.name: Tử Kim Khoáng
places.note: Purple-gold ore, the colour of storm light.

events.text: Purple-gold ore, the colour of storm light, is dug at Tử Kim.

places.name: Vũ Hoa Khoáng
places.note: Rain-flower pebbles, said to be flowers that fell as rain while a master preached; the richest ground of the sixteen (land density 1.87). In Thính Vũ's land of rain.

events.text: Rain-flower pebbles, said to be flowers that fell as rain while a master preached, are found at Vũ Hoa; Thính Vũ keeps the mine.

places.name: Liệt Khuyết Phong
places.note: Lý Bạch, Mộng du Thiên Mỗ: liệt khuyết phích lịch, khâu loan băng thôi (lightning and thunder, and the ridges crumble)

events.text: Khải Lôi's disciples climb Liệt Khuyết Phong in storms to invite the lightning; a third of them come down.
Thính Vũ's disciples drill on Liệt Khuyết Phong in thunderstorms; the villagers below count the lightning and the disciples both.

places.name: Đả Diệp Lâm
places.note: Tô Thức: xuyên lâm đả diệp thanh (rain piercing the forest, beating the leaves), the line of Xuyên Lâm Môn nearby

places.name: Kinh Lôi Mạch
places.note: In Kinh Trập Sơn, the mountains of the thunder that wakes the sleepers; within reach of the storm peaks, so it carries Thunder. 5 tiles from Thiên Xu's border.

events.text: Lệ Tiêu Hồn reaches Nguyên Anh in the Tower's soul vaults; Mạnh Dạ Vũ makes him keeper of Kinh Lôi Mạch.
Phượng Minh Cung goes to war with Thính Vũ Lâu for the Kinh Lôi vein.
The Pivot ends the Thunder Vein War: Thính Vũ keeps the vein, and the south remembers.

places.name: Lôi Trạch Thành
places.note: Khải Lôi's river-mouth city, burned by the lightning of Hầu Xuân Lôi's tribulation.

events.text: Khải Lôi Môn builds Lôi Trạch Thành at the river mouth below its mountains.
A year after the tribulation burned Lôi Trạch Thành, its people move up the valley to Không Mông Thành.

places.name: Thu Phần Các
places.note: Lý Hạ: thu phần quỷ xướng Bão gia thi, ghosts sing old poems in the autumn graves. A bamboo hill 10 tiles from the ruins of Lôi Trạch Thành.

events.text: Lý Hận Bích founds Thu Phần Các among the graves of Lôi Trạch Thành, where ghosts sing old poems in autumn, and swears it to Thính Vũ Lâu.

residents.name: Lý Hận Bích
residents.role: Founder and head of Thu Phần Các (960), soul arts and grave wards among the graves of Lôi Trạch Thành (ma đạo)

places.name: Phục Hổ Cương
places.note: A tiger-kind beast's ridge on the Kinh Trập highland, where the storms wake the hills.

regions.name: Đan Huyệt Châu
regions.image: Sơn Hải Kinh: the phoenix is born on Mount Đan Huyệt; here the caves are volcanic vents

famous_sites.name: Phù Tang Cảnh
famous_sites.note: Sơn Hải Kinh: in the hot valley stands the Phù Tang tree, where the ten suns bathe. Its gate is on the island Dục Nhật Đảo, where the sun bathes.

fallen_sects.name: Xích Thành Môn
fallen_sects.cause: turned to burning villages; destroyed by Phượng Minh under writ. Phần Vũ Đường (1020) later revives its fire arts in the same vents

events.text: The young Hùng Phần Vũ founds Phần Vũ Đường in the vents where Xích Thành once stood; Phượng Minh lends it the Xích Hà Kỳ.
Phần Vũ Đường's disciples sit in the vents until their feathers burn and walk out reborn; the first of them dies trying.

residents.name: Hùng Phần Vũ
residents.role: Head of Phần Vũ Đường, body tempering in the volcanic vents

seat_of.name: Phần Vũ Đường
seat_of.craft: body tempering in the volcanic vents
seat_of.note: The phoenix burns its own feathers to be reborn; here, in the vents of Mount Đan Huyệt

places.name: Ngũ Thải Thành
places.note: Sơn Hải Kinh: the bird of Mount Đan Huyệt is five-coloured, the phoenix

events.text: Xích Thành Môn builds Ngũ Thải Thành on the coast of Đan Huyệt Châu.
Hùng Phần Vũ is born in Ngũ Thải Thành; a red feather falls on his cradle.
Đỗ Tinh Hà calls the Pirate Purge; Phượng Minh's and Lạc Hà's fleets sail under the Pivot's writ, and Thạch Cơ Thành rises around their stone jetty.
Thạch Cơ Thành's stone jetty cracks in a storm; Phượng Minh rebuilds it with stone from the ruins of Xích Thành.
Mulberry fields planted in the red soil at Tang Điền feed the silkworms of the south.
In the War of the Vermilion Caves, the villagers of Cúc Viên hide Phượng Minh's scouts among the chrysanthemums.
The mulberry shade at Tang Âm becomes the resting place of the silk caravans.
The lake at Hồ Tâm rises and falls with the tide, though it touches no sea; Phượng Minh's scholars cannot say why.
Thôn Hải's raiders carry off the whole village of Lô Châu; only the reed cutters hidden in the marsh escape.
Captives freed from Thôn Hải's hold return to Lô Châu and rebuild it reed by reed.

places.name: Đan Thạch Khoáng
places.note: Red stone from the phoenix's cinnabar land, Đan Huyệt Châu.

events.text: Red stone from Đan Thạch is cut for Xích Thành's walls.

places.name: Dục Nhật Đảo
places.note: Sơn Hải Kinh: in the far south-east the suns bathe in the sea before they rise

events.text: Mạc Quy Khư, a Kết Đan cultivator of 240, enters the gate of Phù Tang Cảnh on Dục Nhật Đảo at its first recorded opening; the Thiên Nguyên calendar counts its years from that day.
The first fishers of the gulf see the sun rise out of the sea at Dục Nhật Đảo, and believe it bathes there every night.
Mạc Quy Khư comes to live on Dục Nhật Đảo by the gate of Phù Tang Cảnh, and never leaves it again.
Pilgrims come by boat to Dục Nhật Đảo to ask the hermit Mạc Quy Khư about the world before the sects; he answers one question a year.

residents.name: Mạc Quy Khư
residents.role: The oldest living person (age 1,440): a hermit on the island by the gate of Phù Tang Cảnh, who remembers the world before the sects

places.name: Đồ Nam Đảo
places.note: Trang Tử: the great Bằng rises ninety thousand li, then sets out for the south

events.text: The great Bằng is said to rest on Đồ Nam Đảo before its flight to the south.

places.name: Xích Thành Môn
places.note: The red-cliff gate Phượng Minh destroyed under Thiên Xu's writ.

events.text: Tôn Hà Khởi founds Xích Thành Môn among the red cliffs and vents of Đan Huyệt Châu, where the rock rises like a rosy cloud.
Xích Thành Môn weaves its war banner, the Xích Hà Kỳ, from fire-silk spun in the vents.
Tôn Hà Khởi dies; his heir Chu Liệt Nhật turns Xích Thành Môn to burning villages to feed its fire arts.
Phượng Minh destroys Xích Thành Môn with Chu Liệt Nhật; Đan Huyệt Châu and Ngũ Thải Thành pass to Phượng Minh, and the Xích Hà Kỳ hangs in its hall.

places.name: Thôn Hải Môn
places.note: The pirates' hold on an islet of the southern gulf.

events.text: Ô Kình Hải gathers pirates on an islet of the southern gulf and founds Thôn Hải Môn, the Gate That Swallows the Sea.
The Purge ends at Thôn Hải Môn: Ô Kình Hải dies on his islet and his sabre Kình Nha is lost in the burning hold.

places.name: Vạn Xà Lâm
places.note: Deep jungle at the far end of Đan Huyệt Châu, the farthest lair from any town.

places.name: Chu Sa Tuyền
places.note: A red hot spring in the jungle of Đan Huyệt Châu, the phoenix's cinnabar land.

places.name: Chúc Dung Khẩu
places.note: Named for the fire god; a vent on the east coast of Đan Huyệt Châu.
